subproblems.title: Orthonormal frame (ν, σ) of Q adapted to a unit vector ν ∈ Q, with σ an orthonormal basis of Q ∩ ν^⊥
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q ⊆ ℝ^P = Euclid P be a linear subspace of dimension n + 1 (Module.finrank ℝ Q = n + 1), and let ν ∈ Q with |ν| = 1. Then there is a family σ = (σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}) : Fin n → ℝ^P such that (i) σ is orthonormal; (ii) span(range σ) = Q ∩ ν^⊥ (Lean: Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range σ) = Q ⊓ (ℝ ∙ ν)ᗮ); (iii) the family (ν, σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}) = Fin.cons ν σ : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ^P is orthonormal; (iv) σ_i ∈ Q for every i; (v) ⟨ν, σ_i⟩ = 0 for every i (inner ℝ ν (σ i) = 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ν : Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ Q = n + 1 → ν ∈ Q → ‖ν‖ = 1 → ∃ σ : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ σ ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range σ) = Q ⊓ (ℝ ∙ ν)ᗮ ∧ Orthonormal ℝ (Fin.cons ν σ : Fin (n + 1) → Euclid P) ∧ (∀ i, σ i ∈ Q) ∧ ∀ i, inner ℝ ν (σ i) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 1 of the parent proof (dim Q = n + 1, Q = ℝν ⊕ (Q ∩ ν^⊥) orthogonally, so Q ∩ ν^⊥ has an orthonormal basis σ of n vectors and (ν, σ_1, …, σ_n) is an orthonormal basis of Q); Simon Ch. 6, 4.3 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1209–1219: ξ⌞ν is a simple unit (n−1)-vector of T_xM_t = T_xM ∩ ν^⊥), which uses this adapted frame.
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P); ⟨x, y⟩ = inner ℝ x y; |x| = ‖x‖; an n-covector is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n = Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ; an n-vector is an element of MultiVector P n = Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ; ν^⊥ = (ℝ ∙ ν)ᗮ; Fin.cons ν σ is the family (ν, σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}) indexed by Fin (n + 1). Put Q' := Q ⊓ (ℝ ∙ ν)ᗮ = Q ∩ ν^⊥.
1. ν ≠ 0, since |ν| = 1 ≠ 0 = |0|. Hence the line ℝ∙ν has dimension 1 (finrank_span_singleton). Since ν ∈ Q, ℝ∙ν ≤ Q (Submodule.span_singleton_le_iff_mem).
2. dim Q' = n. For subspaces K₁ ≤ K₂ of ℝ^P (K₂ finite-dimensional), dim K₁ + dim(K₁^⊥ ∩ K₂) = dim K₂ (Submodule.finrank_add_inf_finrank_orthogonal; this is the orthogonal decomposition K₂ = K₁ ⊕ (K₁^⊥ ∩ K₂), q = P_{K₁}q + (q − P_{K₁}q)). With K₁ = ℝ∙ν and K₂ = Q, using step 1 and dim Q = n + 1: 1 + dim((ℝ∙ν)ᗮ ⊓ Q) = n + 1. Since (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ ⊓ Q = Q ⊓ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ = Q' (commutativity of ⊓), dim Q' = n.
3. Choice of σ. Q' is a real inner product space of dimension n, so it has an orthonormal basis b = (b_0, …, b_{n−1}) indexed by Fin n: take stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q' (indexed by Fin (finrank ℝ Q')) and reindex it along finrank ℝ Q' = n (OrthonormalBasis.reindex with finCongr). For n = 0 this is the empty family. Define σ_i := b_i, regarded as a vector of ℝ^P.
4. (i) σ is orthonormal: the inclusion Q' → ℝ^P is a linear isometry (Q'.subtypeₗᵢ), and the image of an orthonormal family under a linear isometry is orthonormal (Orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry applied to b.orthonormal).
5. (ii) span(range σ) = Q'. range σ is the image of range b under the inclusion Q'.subtype, so span(range σ) = (span(range b)).map(Q'.subtype) (Submodule.span_image). As b is a basis of Q', span(range b) = ⊤ in Q' (Basis.span_eq for b.toBasis), and ⊤.map(Q'.subtype) = range(Q'.subtype) = Q' (Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype).
6. (iv) and (v). Each σ_i lies in Q' = Q ⊓ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ, hence σ_i ∈ Q, and σ_i ∈ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ, which means ⟨ν, σ_i⟩ = 0 (Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right).
7. (iii) Let ρ := Fin.cons ν σ, so ρ_0 = ν and ρ_{i+1} = σ_i (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ). By orthonormal_iff_ite it suffices to show ⟨ρ_a, ρ_c⟩ = (1 if a = c else 0) for all a, c ∈ Fin (n + 1). Split a and c into 0 and successors (Fin.cases):
   (a) a = c = 0: ⟨ν, ν⟩ = |ν|² = 1.
   (b) a = 0, c = j + 1: ⟨ν, σ_j⟩ = 0 by (v), and 0 ≠ j + 1 (Fin.succ_ne_zero).
   (c) a = i + 1, c = 0: ⟨σ_i, ν⟩ = ⟨ν, σ_i⟩ = 0 (real_inner_comm), and i + 1 ≠ 0.
   (d) a = i + 1, c = j + 1: ⟨σ_i, σ_j⟩ = (1 if i = j else 0) by (i) and orthonormal_iff_ite, and i + 1 = j + 1 ↔ i = j (Fin.succ_inj).
   Hence ρ = Fin.cons ν σ is orthonormal.
8. Steps 4–7 give (i)–(v) for σ. ∎
(For n = 0, σ is the empty family, Q' = 0 and (iii) reduces to |ν| = 1; the argument is uniform in n.)

The following Lean proof was compiled by this decomposition session, inserted at exactly that position in a copy of GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean (Lean 4.35.0-rc3; `#print axioms` = propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; no errors or warnings), and may be used verbatim:
theorem Submission.dor_lmbsf_io_adapted_frame : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ν : Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ Q = n + 1 → ν ∈ Q → ‖ν‖ = 1 → ∃ σ : Fin n → Euclid P, Orthonormal ℝ σ ∧ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range σ) = Q ⊓ (ℝ ∙ ν)ᗮ ∧ Orthonormal ℝ (Fin.cons ν σ : Fin (n + 1) → Euclid P) ∧ (∀ i, σ i ∈ Q) ∧ ∀ i, inner ℝ ν (σ i) = 0 := by
  intro P n Q ν hQ hνQ hν
  set Q' : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P) := Q ⊓ (ℝ ∙ ν)ᗮ with hQ'def
  have hν0 : ν ≠ 0 := by
    intro h; rw [h, norm_zero] at hν; exact zero_ne_one hν
  have hle : (ℝ ∙ ν) ≤ Q := (Submodule.span_singleton_le_iff_mem ν Q).2 hνQ
  have hdim : Module.finrank ℝ Q' = n := by
    have h1 := Submodule.finrank_add_inf_finrank_orthogonal hle
    rw [finrank_span_singleton hν0, hQ] at h1
    have : Q' = (ℝ ∙ ν)ᗮ ⊓ Q := inf_comm _ _
    rw [this]; omega
  let b : OrthonormalBasis (Fin n) ℝ Q' := (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ Q').reindex (finCongr hdim)
  let σ : Fin n → Euclid P := fun i => (b i : Euclid P)
  have hσ : Orthonormal ℝ σ := b.orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry Q'.subtypeₗᵢ
  have hσmem : ∀ i, σ i ∈ Q' := fun i => (b i).2
  have hσspan : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range σ) = Q' := by
    have hrange : Set.range σ = Q'.subtype '' Set.range b := by
      ext x; simp [σ]
    have htop : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range b) = ⊤ := by simpa using b.toBasis.span_eq
    rw [hrange, Submodule.span_image, htop, Submodule.map_top, Submodule.range_subtype]
  have hσQ : ∀ i, σ i ∈ Q := fun i => (hσmem i).1
  have hνσ : ∀ i, inner ℝ ν (σ i) = 0 := fun i =>
    (Submodule.mem_orthogonal_singleton_iff_inner_right).1 (hσmem i).2
  refine ⟨σ, hσ, hσspan, ?_, hσQ, hνσ⟩
  rw [orthonormal_iff_ite] at hσ ⊢
  intro i j
  refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun i' => ?_) i <;> refine Fin.cases ?_ (fun j' => ?_) j
  · simp [hν]
  · simp [hνσ j', (Fin.succ_ne_zero j').symm]
  · simp [real_inner_comm, hνσ i', Fin.succ_ne_zero i']
  · simp [hσ i' j']
proof_key_steps: ν ≠ 0, so dim(ℝ∙ν) = 1 and ℝ∙ν ≤ Q because ν ∈ Q.
Submodule.finrank_add_inf_finrank_orthogonal: 1 + dim((ℝ∙ν)ᗮ ⊓ Q) = n + 1, so Q' = Q ⊓ (ℝ∙ν)ᗮ has dimension n.
Take an orthonormal basis b of Q' indexed by Fin n (stdOrthonormalBasis reindexed) and σ_i := ↑b_i.
σ is orthonormal (Orthonormal.comp_linearIsometry with Q'.subtypeₗᵢ) and span(range σ) = map Q'.subtype ⊤ = Q'.
σ_i ∈ Q' gives σ_i ∈ Q and ⟨ν, σ_i⟩ = 0.
Fin.cons ν σ is orthonormal: check ⟨ρ_a, ρ_c⟩ = δ_ac by Fin.cases on a and c, using |ν| = 1, ⟨ν, σ_j⟩ = 0 and orthonormality of σ.

subproblems.title: An n-covector on vectors spanned by an orthonormal n-frame is det(⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩) times its value on the frame
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) (indexed by Fin n) be an orthonormal family in ℝᴾ = Euclid P and let b = (b₁, …, bₙ) be a family in ℝᴾ with bⱼ ∈ span{τ₁, …, τₙ} for every j. Then for every n-covector α of ℝᴾ (α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n, a continuous alternating n-linear form), α(b₁, …, bₙ) = det(𝒜)·α(τ₁, …, τₙ), where 𝒜 is the n×n real matrix 𝒜ᵢⱼ := ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩ (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ b : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (∀ j, b j ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ)) → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, α b = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j)).det * α τ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: the first half of Step 2 of the parent proof (every covector β restricted to Q, the alternating map β.compLinearMap Q.subtype, is a multiple of the determinant in the basis τ, AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det, so β(ρ) = det(m)·β(τ)), stated for an arbitrary orthonormal n-frame τ and an n-family b in L = span(range τ). This exact frozen type is already comparator-accepted as Submission.dgoj_covector_eq_det_mul_of_mem_span (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.epsilon_regularity-a1.graph_cycle_regular-a1.graph_orientation_jacobian-a1.covector_frame_det-a1) and is reused here by its identical Lean type; the proof below is the one it was accepted with.
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P); ⟨x, y⟩ = inner ℝ x y; |x| = ‖x‖; an n-covector is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n = Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ; an n-vector is an element of MultiVector P n = Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ; ν^⊥ = (ℝ ∙ ν)ᗮ; Fin.cons ν σ is the family (ν, σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}) indexed by Fin (n + 1). L := span ℝ (range τ) ⊆ ℝᴾ; for c ∈ L, ↑c is the underlying ambient vector.
1. A basis of L indexed by Fin n. An orthonormal family is linearly independent (Orthonormal.linearIndependent), so τ is a basis of its span: e := Module.Basis.span hτ.linearIndependent is a basis (e₁, …, eₙ) of L with ↑eᵢ = τᵢ (Module.Basis.span_apply).
2. Restriction of α to L. Let α_L := α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap L.subtype, i.e. α_L(c₁, …, cₙ) := α(↑c₁, …, ↑cₙ) for cᵢ ∈ L; it is an alternating n-linear form on L. Put b'ⱼ := ⟨bⱼ, hbⱼ⟩ ∈ L (hypothesis). Then α(b) = α_L(b') and α(τ) = α(↑e) = α_L(e) (by unfolding, using ↑eᵢ = τᵢ).
3. Alternating n-forms on the n-dimensional space L with basis e are multiples of the basis determinant: α_L = α_L(e) • det_e (AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det). Evaluating at b' gives α_L(b') = α_L(e)·det_e(b').
4. The coordinate matrix. det_e(b') = det M with Mᵢⱼ := e.repr(b'ⱼ)ᵢ (Module.Basis.det_apply, Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply). We claim Mᵢⱼ = ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩. Indeed b'ⱼ = Σₗ Mₗⱼ • eₗ (Module.Basis.sum_repr); taking underlying vectors (Submodule.coe_sum, Submodule.coe_smul) gives bⱼ = Σₗ Mₗⱼ • τₗ, and taking the inner product with τᵢ and using orthonormality, ⟨τᵢ, Σₗ Mₗⱼ τₗ⟩ = Mᵢⱼ (Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype). Hence M = 𝒜.
5. Combining steps 2–4: α(b) = α_L(b') = α_L(e)·det_e(b') = α(τ)·det 𝒜 = det(𝒜)·α(τ). ∎
(The argument is uniform in n; for n = 0 both sides reduce to α of the empty family, det of the empty matrix being 1.)
Formalization note (supplementary; the numbered proof above is complete): no new proof work. This exact declaration is already comparator-accepted (candidate commit 73310ec921452a01670f397b34d1cf3cd7135598 of DAG node ...graph_orientation_jacobian-a1.covector_frame_det-a1) with the following Lean proof, which this decomposition session recompiled at the same insertion point of a copy of GMT/Ch07/Submission.lean together with its consumer frame_sign (Lean 4.35.0-rc3; `#print axioms` = propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound):
theorem Submission.dgoj_covector_eq_det_mul_of_mem_span : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (τ b : Fin n → Euclid P), Orthonormal ℝ τ → (∀ j, b j ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ)) → ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, α b = (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j)).det * α τ := by
  intro P n τ b hτ hb α
  set L := Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ)
  -- `τ` is a basis `e` of `L`
  let e : Module.Basis (Fin n) ℝ L := Module.Basis.span hτ.linearIndependent
  have he : ∀ i, (e i : Euclid P) = τ i := fun i => by
    rw [Module.Basis.span_apply hτ.linearIndependent i]
  -- the restriction `α_L` of `α` to `L`
  let αL : L [⋀^Fin n]→ₗ[ℝ] ℝ := α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap L.subtype
  let b' : Fin n → L := fun j => ⟨b j, hb j⟩
  have h1 : α b = αL b' := rfl
  have h2 : α τ = αL e := by
    show α τ = α (fun i => (e i : Euclid P))
    congr 1
    funext i
    exact (he i).symm
  -- coordinates of `b'` in `e` are the inner products with `τ`
  have hrepr : ∀ i j, e.repr (b' j) i = inner ℝ (τ i) (b j) := by
    intro i j
    have hs : (b j : Euclid P) = ∑ l, e.repr (b' j) l • τ l := by
      have := congrArg (Subtype.val) (e.sum_repr (b' j))
      simp only [Submodule.coe_sum, Submodule.coe_smul, he] at this
      exact this.symm
    rw [hs, hτ.inner_right_fintype]
  have hmat : e.toMatrix b' = Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (b j) := by
    ext i j
    rw [Module.Basis.toMatrix_apply, hrepr, Matrix.of_apply]
  -- `α_L = α_L(e) • det_e`
  have h3 : αL b' = αL e * e.det b' := by
    conv_lhs => rw [AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det e αL]
    rfl
  rw [h1, h2, h3, Module.Basis.det_apply, hmat, mul_comm]
proof_key_steps: τ orthonormal ⇒ linearly independent ⇒ basis e := Module.Basis.span of L = span(range τ) with ↑eᵢ = τᵢ.
Restrict α to L: α_L := α.toAlternatingMap.compLinearMap L.subtype; α(b) = α_L(b') and α(τ) = α_L(e).
AlternatingMap.eq_smul_basis_det: α_L = α_L(e)·det_e, so α(b) = α(τ)·det_e(b').
det_e(b') = det of the coordinate matrix, whose (i,j) entry is ⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩ by expanding bⱼ = Σₗ cₗ τₗ and orthonormality.
Hence α(b) = det(⟨τᵢ, bⱼ⟩)·α(τ).

subproblems.title: A unit orientation of Q equals ± evaluation at any orthonormal frame in Q (orthonormal change of frame has determinant ±1)
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ, let Q ⊆ ℝ^P be a linear subspace, let ζ be an m-vector (ζ ∈ MultiVector P m, a continuous linear functional on m-covectors) which is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q: there is an orthonormal τ : Fin m → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q and either ζ(β) = β(τ) for every m-covector β or ζ(β) = −β(τ) for every m-covector β), and let ρ : Fin m → ℝ^P be an orthonormal family with ρ_j ∈ Q for every j. Then either ζ(β) = β(ρ) for every m-covector β, or ζ(β) = −β(ρ) for every m-covector β.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ζ : MultiVector P m) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ρ : Fin m → Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q → Orthonormal ℝ ρ → (∀ j, ρ j ∈ Q) → (∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) m, ζ β = β ρ) ∨ ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) m, ζ β = -β ρ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 of the parent proof (the sign lemma, parent Step 0(a): a change between orthonormal frames of Q has determinant ε₀ = ±1, so ζ(β) = ε₁β(τ) = ε₁ε₀β(ρ) with a sign independent of β); Simon Ch. 6, 1.1 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 28–30: ω₁∧⋯∧ωₙ(v₁, …, vₙ) = det(ωᵢ(vⱼ))) and 4.3 (lines 1209–1219). It uses the sibling covector_det (Submission.dgoj_covector_eq_det_mul_of_mem_span).
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P); ⟨x, y⟩ = inner ℝ x y; |x| = ‖x‖; an n-covector is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n = Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ; an n-vector is an element of MultiVector P n = Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ; ν^⊥ = (ℝ ∙ ν)ᗮ; Fin.cons ν σ is the family (ν, σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}) indexed by Fin (n + 1).
1. Unfold the hypothesis IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q: there is τ : Fin m → ℝ^P, orthonormal, with span(range τ) = Q, and (Case ε₁ = 1) ζ(β) = β(τ) for every m-covector β, or (Case ε₁ = −1) ζ(β) = −β(τ) for every β.
2. Change-of-frame formula. Since span(range τ) = Q and ρ_j ∈ Q, every ρ_j ∈ span(range τ). Let M be the m×m real matrix M_{ij} := ⟨τ_i, ρ_j⟩ (Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (ρ j)). By the sibling covector_det applied to the orthonormal frame τ and the family b := ρ: β(ρ) = det(M)·β(τ) for every m-covector β.
3. Parseval in span(range τ). For x ∈ ℝ^P and y ∈ span(range τ): ⟨x, y⟩ = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, x⟩⟨τ_i, y⟩. Proof: write y = Σ_l c_l τ_l (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun). By orthonormality ⟨τ_i, y⟩ = c_i (Orthonormal.inner_right_fintype), and by linearity ⟨x, y⟩ = Σ_l c_l⟨x, τ_l⟩ (inner_sum, inner_smul_right) = Σ_l ⟨τ_l, x⟩ c_l (real_inner_comm, commutativity of ·) = Σ_l ⟨τ_l, x⟩⟨τ_l, y⟩.
4. M is orthogonal: MᵀM = I. For j, k ∈ Fin m, (MᵀM)_{jk} = Σ_i M_{ij}M_{ik} = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, ρ_j⟩⟨τ_i, ρ_k⟩ = ⟨ρ_j, ρ_k⟩ (step 3 with x = ρ_j and y = ρ_k ∈ span(range τ)) = (1 if j = k else 0), because ρ is orthonormal (orthonormal_iff_ite).
5. det M = ±1. det(M)·det(M) = det(Mᵀ)·det(M) = det(MᵀM) = det(I) = 1 (Matrix.det_transpose, Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_one). Hence (det M − 1)(det M + 1) = det(M)² − 1 = 0, so ε₀ := det M = 1 or ε₀ = −1. (This is the parent's 'orthogonal change between orthonormal bases has determinant ±1', cf. OrthonormalBasis.det_to_matrix_orthonormalBasis_real.)
6. Conclusion, by the four sign combinations; in each case fix an arbitrary m-covector β and use step 2, β(ρ) = ε₀β(τ):
   (a) ε₁ = 1, ε₀ = 1: ζ(β) = β(τ) = 1·β(τ) = β(ρ). First alternative.
   (b) ε₁ = 1, ε₀ = −1: β(ρ) = −β(τ), so ζ(β) = β(τ) = −β(ρ). Second alternative.
   (c) ε₁ = −1, ε₀ = 1: β(ρ) = β(τ), so ζ(β) = −β(τ) = −β(ρ). Second alternative.
   (d) ε₁ = −1, ε₀ = −1: β(ρ) = −β(τ), so ζ(β) = −β(τ) = β(ρ). First alternative.
   Since ε₁ and ε₀ do not depend on β, in each case the same alternative holds for every β. ∎
(For m = 0, τ and ρ are the empty family, M is the empty matrix with det M = 1, and the argument is uniform.)

theorem Submission.dor_lmbsf_io_orientation_frame_sign : ∀ (P m : ℕ) (ζ : MultiVector P m) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ρ : Fin m → Euclid P), IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q → Orthonormal ℝ ρ → (∀ j, ρ j ∈ Q) → (∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) m, ζ β = β ρ) ∨ ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) m, ζ β = -β ρ := by
  intro P m ζ Q ρ hζ hρ hρQ
  obtain ⟨τ, hτ, hspan, hsign⟩ := hζ
  set M : Matrix (Fin m) (Fin m) ℝ := Matrix.of fun i j => inner ℝ (τ i) (ρ j) with hM
  have hρspan : ∀ j, ρ j ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) := fun j => hspan ▸ hρQ j
  have hdet : ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) m, β ρ = M.det * β τ :=
    Submission.dgoj_covector_eq_det_mul_of_mem_span P m τ ρ hτ hρspan
  have hparseval : ∀ x y : Euclid P, y ∈ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range τ) →
      inner ℝ x y = ∑ i, inner ℝ (τ i) x * inner ℝ (τ i) y := by
    intro x y hy
    obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := (Submodule.mem_span_range_iff_exists_fun ℝ).1 hy
    simp only [hτ.inner_right_fintype, inner_sum, inner_smul_right]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun i _ => ?_)
    rw [real_inner_comm, mul_comm]
  have hMM : M.transpose * M = 1 := by
    ext j k
    rw [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.one_apply]
    simp only [Matrix.transpose_apply, hM, Matrix.of_apply]
    rw [← hparseval (ρ j) (ρ k) (hρspan k)]
    exact orthonormal_iff_ite.1 hρ j k
  have hdet2 : M.det * M.det = 1 := by
    have := congrArg Matrix.det hMM
    rwa [Matrix.det_mul, Matrix.det_transpose, Matrix.det_one] at this
  have hpm : M.det = 1 ∨ M.det = -1 := by
    have h0 : (M.det - 1) * (M.det + 1) = 0 := by linear_combination hdet2
    rcases mul_eq_zero.1 h0 with h | h
    · left; linarith
    · right; linarith
  rcases hsign with h | h <;> rcases hpm with hd | hd
  · left; intro β; rw [h, hdet, hd, one_mul]
  · right; intro β; rw [h, hdet, hd]; ring
  · right; intro β; rw [h, hdet, hd, one_mul]
  · left; intro β; rw [h, hdet, hd]; ring
proof_key_steps: Unfold IsUnitOrientationOf ζ Q: orthonormal τ with span(range τ) = Q and ζ(β) = ε₁β(τ), ε₁ ∈ {1, −1}.
ρ_j ∈ span(range τ); by covector_det, β(ρ) = det(M)·β(τ) with M_{ij} = ⟨τ_i, ρ_j⟩.
Parseval for y ∈ span(range τ): ⟨x, y⟩ = Σ_i ⟨τ_i, x⟩⟨τ_i, y⟩, hence MᵀM = I by orthonormality of ρ.
det(M)² = det(MᵀM) = 1, so ε₀ := det M ∈ {1, −1}.
Case analysis on (ε₁, ε₀): ζ(β) = ε₁ε₀β(ρ) for all β, giving the first alternative if ε₁ε₀ = 1 and the second if ε₁ε₀ = −1.

subproblems.title: Interior-product evaluation: (ν♭ ∧ α)(ν, σ) = α(σ) for a unit ν orthogonal to σ
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let ν ∈ ℝ^P with |ν| = 1, let σ = (σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}) : Fin n → ℝ^P with ⟨ν, σ_i⟩ = 0 for every i, and let α be an n-covector of ℝ^P (α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n). Let ν♭ ∧ α := ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin((innerSL ℝ ν).smulRight α), the (n+1)-covector (ν♭∧α)(v_0, …, v_n) = Σ_{i=0}^{n} (−1)^i ⟨ν, v_i⟩ α(v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_n). Then (ν♭∧α)(ν, σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}) = α(σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}), where (ν, σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}) = Fin.cons ν σ : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ^P.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Euclid P) (σ : Fin n → Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), ‖ν‖ = 1 → (∀ i, inner ℝ ν (σ i) = 0) → ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ ν).smulRight α) (Fin.cons ν σ : Fin (n + 1) → Euclid P) = α σ
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: Step 3 of the parent proof (wedge expansion); Simon Ch. 6, 4.3 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 1209–1219: ⟨v⌞w, a⟩ = ⟨v, w ∧ a⟩, the interior product used to orient the slice).
Notation: ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P); ⟨x, y⟩ = inner ℝ x y; |x| = ‖x‖; an n-covector is an element of Covector (Euclid P) n = Euclid P [⋀^Fin n]→L[ℝ] ℝ; an n-vector is an element of MultiVector P n = Covector (Euclid P) n →L[ℝ] ℝ; ν^⊥ = (ℝ ∙ ν)ᗮ; Fin.cons ν σ is the family (ν, σ_0, …, σ_{n−1}) indexed by Fin (n + 1).
1. Expansion formula. For F : ℝ^P →L[ℝ] Covector (Euclid P) n and v : Fin (n + 1) → ℝ^P, (alternatizeUncurryFin F)(v) = Σ_{i : Fin (n+1)} (−1)^i • F(v_i)(removeNth i v) (ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_apply), where removeNth i v is v with the i-th entry deleted. Here F = (innerSL ℝ ν).smulRight α, so F(w) = ⟨ν, w⟩ • α (ContinuousLinearMap.smulRight_apply, innerSL_apply_apply) and F(w)(u) = ⟨ν, w⟩·α(u).
2. Take v := Fin.cons ν σ, so v_0 = ν and v_{j+1} = σ_j (Fin.cons_zero, Fin.cons_succ). Split the sum over Fin (n + 1) into the term i = 0 and the terms i = j + 1, j ∈ Fin n (Fin.sum_univ_succ).
3. The term i = 0 equals (−1)^0·⟨ν, ν⟩·α(removeNth 0 v). Here removeNth 0 v = Fin.tail (Fin.cons ν σ) = σ (Fin.removeNth_zero, Fin.tail_cons) and ⟨ν, ν⟩ = |ν|² = 1. So this term is α(σ).
4. For i = j + 1 the term equals (−1)^{j+1}·⟨ν, σ_j⟩·α(removeNth (j+1) v) = 0, because ⟨ν, σ_j⟩ = 0 by hypothesis.
5. Summing, (ν♭∧α)(Fin.cons ν σ) = α(σ) + 0 = α(σ). For n = 0 the sum consists of the i = 0 term only and the same computation applies. ∎

theorem Submission.dor_lmbsf_io_wedge_eval_cons : ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ν : Euclid P) (σ : Fin n → Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), ‖ν‖ = 1 → (∀ i, inner ℝ ν (σ i) = 0) → ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin ((innerSL ℝ ν).smulRight α) (Fin.cons ν σ : Fin (n + 1) → Euclid P) = α σ := by
  intro P n ν σ α hν hνσ
  rw [ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_apply, Fin.sum_univ_succ]
  simp [Fin.removeNth_zero, Fin.tail_cons, innerSL_apply_apply, hνσ, hν]
proof_key_steps: ContinuousAlternatingMap.alternatizeUncurryFin_apply: (ν♭∧α)(v) = Σ_i (−1)^i ⟨ν, v_i⟩ α(removeNth i v).
With v = Fin.cons ν σ, split off i = 0 by Fin.sum_univ_succ.
The i = 0 term is ⟨ν, ν⟩ α(Fin.tail (Fin.cons ν σ)) = |ν|² α(σ) = α(σ).
Every term i = j + 1 contains ⟨ν, σ_j⟩ = 0.
Hence (ν♭∧α)(ν, σ) = α(σ).
